title: Adaptive segment coalescer and spill-priority heuristic for KV cache
author: Aisha Patel
release_notes: Improves KV cache memory compaction and spill ordering to reduce fragmentation and tail-latency from spill-induced stalls. No API changes.
description:
Context: We observed tail-latency spikes under mixed workloads where small high-priority KV entries were being evicted alongside large cold regions; fragmentation increased spill frequency and I/O contention. This PR implements an adaptive segment coalescer plus a spill-priority heuristic to (1) proactively merge adjacent small/free segments into larger contiguous regions to reduce fragmentation, and (2) order spill candidates by a score that balances size, access recency, and tenant priority so we avoid evicting hot small entries that cause repeated rehydration.

Motivation: reduce background spill I/O, lower p99 generation latency, and improve effective cache utilization without raising memory limits.

Design summary:
- Segment coalescer: lightweight background job that scans slab segment metadata and attempts coalescing opportunities when free-run fragmentation crosses a tunable threshold. Uses exponential backoff and budgeted work per cycle to avoid impacting foreground scheduling.
- Spill-priority heuristic: new scoring function score = w_age*age_rank + w_size*size_rank + w_tenant*tenant_weight + w_frag*fragment_penalty. Scores are normalized per-eviction-window; the evictor picks lowest-scored items first. Tenant weight is higher for dedicated customers to honor isolation SLAs.
- Integrations: coalescer hooks into existing KV allocator and exposes metrics for coalescing cycles, reclaimed_bytes, and rejected_attempts. Evictor changes are pluggable: existing policies remain available via feature flag.
- Safety: coalescer avoids touching segments referenced by in-flight requests using existing segment pinning API. Spill ordering remains conservative: we only escalate ordering when available_disk_bandwidth > threshold to avoid worsening hot-path stalls.

Implementation notes:
- Core changes in kv/allocator/segment_coalescer.{cc,h}, kv/evictor/spill_priority.{cc,h}, and small changes in serving/runtime/cache_manager.{cc} to expose tuning knobs.
- New config flags: kv.coalescer.enabled, kv.coalescer.scan_budget_ms, kv.eviction.spill_priority_weights.
- Unit tests for scoring, plus integration test that simulates hot-small-item churn and verifies p99 and rehydration counts.

Benchmarks:
- Microbench on a mixed cache workload (50% small hot keys, 50% large cold objects) shows: median throughput +2.6%, p95 latency -9%, p99 latency -21% (measured token-gen latency during sustained ingress with KV hits).
- End-to-end internal benchmark with 10 tenants, 2 dedicated: overall spill bytes reduced by 34%, background disk stalls reduced by 48% on average.

Observability: Added metrics: kv_coalesce_cycles_total, kv_coalesce_reclaimed_bytes, kv_spill_score_histogram, kv_spill_order_skipped_due_to_bw. There are dashboards changes in observability-pack (minor) to visualize reclaimed bytes over time.

Testing and CI:
- Ran full unit/integration suite; initial CI showed a flaky test in allocator when coalescer ran concurrently with heavy pin/unpin; fixed with an extra fast-path check to avoid redundant coalesce attempts, re-ran CI (all green).
- Stress test: 24h soak with synthetic churn, no memory regressions and stable p99.

Rollout plan: feature flag off by default. Canary rollout to internal dedicated cluster (5% traffic) for 48h, monitor kv_coalesce_reclaimed_bytes and p99. If regression observed, rollback via flag.

Related work: follows up on ENG-2986 (kv fragmentation telemetry) and complements prior spillback-pressure work (PR 33102).

Commits: ["core: add segment coalescer scheduler and basic heuristics","kv: introduce spill priority scoring and ordering","config: expose tunables for coalescer and spill weights","tests: add unit tests for score function and coalescer","bench: workload harness for mixed hot/cold KV workload","docs: add runtime tuning guide for kv coalescer"].

Changed files (high level): ["kv/allocator/segment_coalescer.cc","kv/allocator/segment_coalescer.h","kv/evictor/spill_priority.cc","kv/evictor/spill_priority.h","serving/runtime/cache_manager.cc","configs/defaults.yaml","tests/kv/coalesce_spill_integration_test.cc"].

Review conversation:
- Ethan Zhang (reviewer): "Nice approach. My main concern is the coalescer budget interfering with CPU-stealing for inference. Can we ensure coalescer work runs on a lower QoS thread pool?"
- Author (Aisha): "Yes — coalescer is scheduled on the background maintenance pool and we added explicit yield points; updated code to use maintenance_worker token and added tests to assert no work runs on latency-critical pools."
- Ethan: "+1 after the maintenance pool change and a nit about a log line level (info->debug)."
- Marta Gomez (reviewer): "Can we expose tenant-weight overrides via the console for quick mitigation?"
- Author: "Added kv.eviction.tenant_weights as a JSON map in defaults.yaml and documented it in the runtime tuning guide. Console exposure will be a follow-up (ENG-4150)."
- Liam O'Connor: "I ran the 24h stress and saw one boundary case where coalescer thrashes on alternating free ranges; suggest a hysteresis flag."
- Author: "Added coalescer.hysteresis_threshold_ms and a small hysteresis window to avoid immediate re-coalescing; updated tests."

CI narrative: Initial CI run had 1 flaky allocator test failure; rerun succeeded after fix. Linting and security scans clean.

Merge outcome: squashed and merged to main; change log entry added.

Impact: This PR reduces fragmentation-related spill events and lowers tail latencies for generation-heavy workloads without changing external APIs.

Rollout notes: Enable feature flag in canary for 48h, if stable progressively enable for dedicated pools. Monitoring should watch kv_coalesce_reclaimed_bytes, kv_spill_score_histogram, and serving p99 token latencies.
